question.leadin: You probably know more about Hawaiian mythology than you think you do.
question.text: The menehune (MEN-eh-HOO-neh) are the Hawaiian equivalents of these little people that, in Norse mythology, make excellent smiths.
question.clue: Orange Alternative claimed there could be "no freedom without" what creatures? These creatures were graffitied in spots where Polish authorities had painted over anti-government messages.

swap.leadin: The 1569 Union of Lublin joined this region with Lithuania, and it underwent three partitions before 1800.
swap.text: Name this country, which was invaded by the Nazis on September 1, 1939 to start World War II. The Soviets invaded this country two weeks later.
swap.clue: This country's cavalry never actually attacked tanks with lances at Krojanty during an invasion.

question.leadin: One of these events in August 1980 was sparked by the firing of Anna Walentynowicz ["VAL-en-TIN-oh-WITCH"].
question.text: Name this type of action undertaken by workers at the Lenin Shipyards under the leadership of electrical engineer Lech Walesa ["WUH-leh-SUH"]. Arthur Scargill led several of these actions for British coal miners.
question.answerHtml: strikes [accept labor strikes or strike actions; prompt on protests or walkouts or factory occupations or industrial actions]
question.clue: The headline "Crisis? What Crisis?" was used to criticize James Callaghan's handling of a wave of these events that became known as the "Winter of Discontent."

swap.text: This first chairman of Solidarity became the first directly-elected President of Poland in 1990 and won the 1983 Nobel Peace Prize.
swap.clue: This man mourned his successor in 2010 after that successor died in a Smolensk airport plane crash.

question.text: The Union of Lublin was signed after one ruler of this name, the last Jagiellon, left no heirs. The third Polish ruler of this name was a member of the House of Vasa who conquered large areas of Russia before being driven back.
question.clue: Albert Hohenzollern was made a Duke by a ruler of this name in the Prussian Homage.

swap.text: Sigismund II's inability to bear a child resulted in the formation of this personal union partitioned by Prussia, Austria, and Russia. Napoleon later revived a small part of it as the Grand Duchy of Warsaw.
swap.clue: Monarchs agreed to the Henrician Articles and made individual commitments called the pacta conventa on becoming rulers of this country.

question.leadin: This country united with its neighbor Lithuania under the 1569 Union of Lublin.
question.text: Name this country, whose 1573 Compact of Warsaw guaranteed religious freedom to all free people within its borders.
question.clue: This country was united in the Union of Lublin while it was ruled by the Jagiellonians.

swap.leadin: During its country's first free election, this party used a modified version of a poster for the movie High Noon.
swap.text: Name this trade union founded by Lech Walesa that, in 1989, secured semi-free elections in a Warsaw Pact country.
swap.clue: Partly inspired by the 1971 essay Theses on Hope and Hopelessness, this organization secured its seat in government in a free election held in 1990, which led to a successful implementation of "shock therapy."

question.leadin: Raging from 1733 to 1738, it was sparked by the death of Augustus the Strong and the competition between sjems to name an heir.
question.text: Name this conflict, ended by the Treaty of Vienna, which put Frederick Augustus on the throne of the European kingdom that had once been joined with Lithuania in the Union of Lublin.
question.clue: The person who led the Confederation of Dzikow had previously held the job in question under Swedish domination and was the father-in-law of Louis XV.

swap.leadin: During the reign of Augustus III, only one of these bodies succeeded in passing any laws at all.
swap.text: Name these Polish legislative bodies. A "great" one of these bodies passed the Constitution of May 3rd, 1791.
swap.clue: The szlachta class composed the majority of its Chamber of Deputies.

question.leadin: This leader was once suspected of being an informant with the codename "Bolek" for his country's secret police force.
question.text: Name this leader of the trade union Solidarity, who participated in the Round Table Talks with his country's communist government led by Wojciech Jaruzelski.
question.clue: The KOR ("K-O-R") was a predecessor to an organization led by this man, which formed a coalition government with the PUWP.

swap.text: Under the liberum veto rule, any noble could veto an act of the Sejm, the parliament of this country. The Union of Lublin united this country with Lithuania and it was later partitioned three times in the 18th century.
swap.clue: Rulers of this kingdom agreed to a set of "articles" named after Henry of Valois, its first elected king.

question.text: Augustus William of Prussia allegedly died after a broken heart, but really died of a brain tumor, after a crushing defeat in this region. Prussia invaded this region of modern-day Poland to set off the war of Austrian succession.
question.clue: Frederick the Great's 1740 occupation of this region triggered the War of the Austrian Succession.

swap.leadin: One source records how during a rebellion in this city, people who could not pronounce the shibboleth "lentil, wheel, grinds, mill" were executed.
swap.text: Name this city whose German-speaking population revolted in 1312 under a wojt ("vooyt") named Albert. In 1320, Wladyslaw ("v'wa-DISS-wahf") the Elbow-High was crowned king of Poland in this former Polish capitals's Wawel ("VAH-vell") Cathedral.
swap.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

question.text: This Grand Duke of Lithuania and later King of Poland converted the last pagan state in Europe, Lithuania, to Christianity, and then laid the smack-down on the Teutonic Knights at the First Battle of Tannenberg in 1410.
question.answerHtml: Wladyslaw II (accept Jogaila or Jagiello as family name)

swap.leadin: Hugh Trevor-Roper argued that in this century, Spain suffered from a "General Crisis" during a "revolutionary situation" caused by tension between "Court" and "Country."
swap.text: Name this century in which the Habsburgs relinquished claims to the Portuguese throne after the Restoration War. This century saw the end of the Eighty Years' War at the Peace of Munster.
swap.clue: 27 Czech leaders were executed in Prague's Old Town Square during this century, partially as revenge for an earlier event in which Ferdinand II's Catholic representatives were hurled out a window.

question.text: The Swedish monarchy was much more powerful a century earlier when it controlled Poland from 1655 to 1660 in a period known by this name
question.clue: Key precipitating factors of this period include the increased power of the nobility due to Sarmatism and Golden Liberty system, and it saw secondary conflicts like the Second Northern War.

swap.leadin: Polish negotiators drew on earlier legal precedents for a 1466 treaty named for this city, which Frederick II of Brandenburg and Jan Jiskra ("yan YIS-kruh")had failed to mediate.
swap.text: Name this city on the Vistula whose "First Peace" followed the Battle of Grunwald ("GROON-valt"). Poland annexed Royal Prussia at this city's "Second Peace" after the Thirteen Years' War.
swap.answerHtml: Thorn (“torn”) [or Toruń; accept First or Second Peace of Thorn or Toruń]

question.text: This Polish ethnic group targeted by the Germanization program was later one of the few labeled as capable of Germanization by the Nazis, an effort they did little to comply with; nonetheless, many members of this ethnic group centered in Pomerania were expelled along with the Germans after the war.

swap.text: This class promoted their Sarmatian ancestry during the Early Modern period, which they claimed was not held by the commoners of their country. This class increased their power with a set of rules forced on Henry of Valois.
swap.answerHtml: szlachta (“SH’LAKH-tah”) [or Polish nobility, Lithuanian nobility, or Polish-Lithuanian nobility; accept word forms]
swap.clue: These people pushed through a law called Nihil novi and maintained a stranglehold on politics described as "the king reigns but does not govern" through use of the liberum veto.
